evals.prompt: I'm helping a candidate prep for an interview and I have everything you need. ROLE: Senior GTM Strategy Lead, Emerging Products at Northwind Data (B2B data-infrastructure SaaS, ~3,000 employees). JD highlights: own GTM strategy for two new product lines; identify whitespace across land/adopt/expand/renew; run independent analysis in SQL and Tableau; partner-motion design experience required; strong cross-functional influence; AI experience a plus. CANDIDATE (call her Priya): 11 years — 2 years strategy consulting at a top firm, then 9 at a large consumer-tech company in product strategy & ops; built a partner-level revenue model used in carrier negotiations; set annual volume targets with cross-org consensus; proposed a store-surface change credited with a ~$400M ARR uplift; skilled in SQL/Tableau; uses AI tools daily. No classic sales-ops or quota-setting experience. INTERVIEWER: Dan Kovac, Director of Sales Strategy at Northwind — he would be Priya's PEER, both reporting to the same VP. His profile self-describes as 'relentlessly data-driven'; career spine is pricing and monetization roles, with one early-stage-startup chapter. RESEARCH NOTE I already did: Northwind's three stated priorities are enterprise expansion, an AI copilot launch ('Compass'), and reaching profitability; main competitive threat is bundling by a much larger platform vendor. This is a single 60-minute conversation with Dan. Please build the full mock-interview pack: questions categorized by interviewer persona and by question type, tabular, with answer guidance and the rationale for including and categorizing each question.
evals.expected_output: A complete markdown prep pack generated without any clarifying questions, with peer-weighted personas, grounded guidance mapped to Priya's stated stories, and every question carrying type tags, rationale, and a provenance label.
expectations: The first response delivers a complete prep pack in the same message as any questions — it never opens with clarifying questions alone, an intake checklist alone, or a consent request alone. Where an input is missing, the pack is built anyway on a stated assumption and the questions are framed as what would restructure it
No clarifying question is asked before generating (round type, relationship, JD, and CV context were all supplied)
The output is a markdown pack containing persona-organized question-bank tables with columns covering the question, a type tag, answer guidance, and a rationale

A Peer Evaluator persona appears with elevated likelihood explicitly justified by the stated peer relationship, and its bank includes at least one seam/boundary question and one credit-sharing or reciprocity question

A Data-Driven Prober persona is weighted up with reasoning that cites Dan's 'data-driven' self-description, and at least one question asks Priya to defend the ~$400M ARR claim including her personal attribution

The fit snapshot maps the stated JD requirements to Priya's evidence and treats quota-setting/sales-ops as an explicit gap with bridge language, and at least one Skeptic or Pressure question rehearses that exact objection
At least one case or company question is grounded in the supplied research note (Compass launch, profitability push, or the bundling threat) rather than generic strategy
Every question's rationale ends with a provenance label ([grounded], [inferred], or [generic])
The pack ends with an upgrade menu listing concrete missing inputs (e.g., full JD text, full CV document, Dan's full profile) and what each unlocks
The pack explicitly states that the company's published values and documented interview process could not be established from attributable sources, rather than silently omitting the values section

evals.prompt: Interview next week, help me prep. The JD says: 'Operations Manager, Atlas Freight (regional logistics, 800 employees). Own daily terminal operations across 4 sites; drive on-time performance and cost-per-shipment down; lead a team of 12 supervisors; build reporting in Excel/Power BI; 5+ years operations leadership required; Lean/Six Sigma a plus.' My background: 7 years in warehouse and distribution ops, currently a senior shift manager over 3 supervisors; cut mis-pick rate 40% by redesigning the pick path; ran the site's peak-season surge plan two years running; green belt certified; solid Excel, never used Power BI. That's all I have — I don't know anything about who's interviewing me.
evals.expected_output: One compact clarifying exchange (round type + research consent), then a full pack that degrades honestly: no interviewer-read section, round-type persona priors, generic reverse questions, and an upgrade menu.
expectations: The first response delivers a complete prep pack in the same message as any questions — it never opens with clarifying questions alone, an intake checklist alone, or a consent request alone. Where an input is missing, the pack is built anyway on a stated assumption and the questions are framed as what would restructure it

Exactly one clarifying message is sent before generating, containing at most three questions, covering round type/relationship to the interviewer and research-depth consent — and generation proceeds even though interviewer identity remains unknown
No 'Reading the interviewer' section appears in the pack, and no facts about any specific interviewer are invented
Reverse questions are role-generic (about the team, the sites, success criteria) with no fabricated references to a named interviewer

Each stated JD requirement (multi-site operations, on-time/cost metrics, team of 12, Power BI, Lean/Six Sigma) has at least one JD-tagged question, and the 3-supervisors-to-12 and Power BI gaps each get a Skeptic or Pressure question with bridge guidance
The 40% mis-pick claim gets a defend-the-number EXP question whose guidance includes naming the weakest assumption and precise personal attribution
The upgrade menu lists interviewer identity/profile and company research among the unlocks
The pack explicitly states that the company's published values and interview process could not be established from attributable sources, and names the archetype its loop assumptions fall back to

evals.prompt: I have a final-round interview at Stripe for a Product Operations Manager role. Help me get ready.
evals.expected_output: One bundled clarifying exchange, L1 research actually performed (official values/principles, documented loop structure), then an honest gate-only pack: inferred JD questions, a self-assessment fit worksheet, and heavy provenance labeling.
expectations: The first response delivers a complete prep pack in the same message as any questions — it never opens with clarifying questions alone, an intake checklist alone, or a consent request alone. Where an input is missing, the pack is built anyway on a stated assumption and the questions are framed as what would restructure it

At most one clarifying message is sent (covering round detail/relationship, an offer to paste the JD and CV, and research-depth consent), and the pack is generated after that single exchange even if the user supplies nothing further

Web research is actually performed for Stripe's published operating principles/values and its documented interview process rather than answering from model memory, and the Sources section cites what was found
JD-derived questions are labeled [inferred] and the pack states they were built from a researched representative JD for the title
With no CV provided, the fit snapshot appears as a self-assessment worksheet variant with story-selection scaffolds instead of story-mapped guidance
A values/behavioral bank maps questions to the company's actual published principles found in research, by name
The pack ends with an upgrade menu, and no section fabricates a specific interviewer, team, or unverified company fact

The pack states that the final round is typically multiple sessions, runs as a single blended session-mode pack rather than fabricating a per-session schedule, and offers per-session packs in the upgrade menu once the schedule is known

evals.expected_output: A full pack that consumes the handoff: story-mapped [grounded] guidance built on the verified evidence (with the medium-confidence caveat coached), strategy-constrained guidance per weak area, the dossier's named objection given the deepest rehearsal and attributed to the dossier, its risks and employer questions carried into the reverse bank, no prohibited claim asserted anywhere, a Sources note naming the dossier, and a one-line pack_feedback offer at the end.
expectations: The first response delivers a complete prep pack in the same message as any questions — it never opens with clarifying questions alone, an intake checklist alone, or a consent request alone. Where an input is missing, the pack is built anyway on a stated assumption and the questions are framed as what would restructure it

No clarifying question asks for the JD or the candidate's background — the dossier's role_profile and verified evidence already supply them; at most one clarifying message is sent and it covers only what the dossier does not carry (e.g. research-depth consent or interviewer identity)

Guidance built on the dossier's verified_candidate_evidence is story-mapped to those specific claims (the 30+ integrations, the integration playbook, the quarterly roadmap-input sessions) and labeled [grounded] rather than written as story-selection scaffolds

The roadmap-input-sessions claim, flagged medium confidence in the dossier, is coached with its verification caveat named — the guidance tells the candidate to volunteer the limit of inspectable proof rather than leaving it for a prober to extract

The R1 area whose allowed_interview_strategy is 'bridge' is coached as a transferable case with its limit explicitly named, and the area whose strategy is 'acknowledge_gap' (owning a roadmap and prioritization authority) is coached as a plain acknowledgment plus a ramp plan with no invented bridge or adjacent-evidence claim

The dossier's likely_interviewer_objections item (never held the PM title or owned a roadmap) is named as the pack's highest-ROI rehearsal and gets the deepest treatment, and the pack attributes it to the dossier rather than presenting it as the pack's own inference

No prohibited claim is asserted, softened, or implied anywhere in the pack: no guidance, story mapping, or reverse question has the candidate claim she held a PM title, owned a roadmap, or set prioritization for an engineering squad
Both opportunity_risks_to_validate items and both questions_for_employer appear in the reverse-question bank (in substance, not necessarily verbatim), each with a 'why it lands' line
The Sources section states that a tuesday-dossier.md was consumed and names which sections it supplied

The pack ends with an upgrade menu and offers, in one line and without pressure, to emit or update the dossier with a pack_feedback section — it does not emit one unprompted and does not make the offer a condition of anything

The pack does not relitigate the underwriter's conditional_go decision or tell the candidate whether to apply, and nothing in the pack treats the dossier as having been required for the pack to be built

evals.prompt: Second round on Tuesday for Senior Partnerships Manager at Kelverton Rail (UK rail-tech, ~600 staff, they sell scheduling software to train operating companies). The recruiter was unusually specific in her email, quoting it: "The panel is Deepa (VP Partnerships, your future manager) and Ross (Commercial Director). 60 minutes. First 15 minutes we'd like you to present a short POV on where you'd take our operator partnerships over the next 18 months — no slides needed, just talk us through it. Please land on what it means for the operators themselves. Rest is Q&A, and Ross will push on commercials." She also attached the market report their strategy team circulated internally last quarter, which I've read. I've got about four hours of prep time total, spread over the weekend. MY BACKGROUND: 9 years in partnerships, last 4 at a payments company running the ISV channel — took it from 6 partners to 40, roughly £4M of influenced revenue. Before that, 5 years in transport consulting (bus and light rail network planning, so I know the operator world from the other side). Never sold into rail specifically and never carried a direct quota, only influenced revenue.
evals.expected_output: A pack with a dedicated build section for the pre-declared POV (grounded in the supplied report, theses each with a concession, a differentiation strategy against the report's own consensus, and the operator-benefit close the recruiter named), a prep triage sized to four hours, panel-weighted personas for the two named interviewers, and any beyond-spec addition arriving as a labeled offer.
expectations: The first response delivers a complete prep pack in the same message as any questions — it never opens with clarifying questions alone, an intake checklist alone, or a consent request alone. Where an input is missing, the pack is built anyway on a stated assumption and the questions are framed as what would restructure it
A dedicated build section exists for the pre-declared POV deliverable — questions alone do not satisfy it, because an announced deliverable is a graded deliverable
The POV section offers 2-3 defensible theses, and each carries an explicit concession rather than being argued as unqualified

The POV section names a differentiation strategy against the supplied market report rather than reciting it, on the reasoning that a document circulated internally is equally available to the panel and to rival candidates — and where the role warrants saying no, an anti-pick appears
The recruiter's named close is honoured: the POV lands on what the direction means for the train operating companies themselves, not only for Kelverton

A prep triage section appears, sized to the stated four hours, ordering the few things worth doing well and tying each to a pack section or question ID, and closing with an explicit line that everything else is insurance
The prep triage is not padded to fill the time — items the candidate should skip are named as skippable rather than dressed up as work

Persona weights reflect a two-person panel with the stated roles: the future manager and a commercial director whose stated behaviour is to push on commercials, with the reasoning shown rather than asserted

The never-carried-a-quota gap and the never-sold-into-rail gap each get a Skeptic or Pressure question with bridge guidance, and the influenced-revenue figure gets a defend-the-number EXP question that coaches precise attribution
The transport-consulting background is used as a genuine adjacency (operator-side domain knowledge) with its limit named, and is never presented as rail sales experience
Every question's rationale ends with a provenance label, and claims about Kelverton that research could not attribute are labeled or dropped rather than asserted
Any section beyond the skill's own spec arrives as a clearly labeled offer with one line on what it would add, rather than being woven into the pack unannounced
The pack ends with an upgrade menu, and the dossier or pack_feedback offer appears as a single unpressured line rather than a precondition
